### 🧱 Engineering Principles

These are the rules I write, review, and architect by. Not aspirational — operational.

```
1.  Correctness before performance. A fast wrong answer is worse than a slow right one.
2.  Explicit over implicit. If the reader has to guess, the code has failed.
3.  Errors are data. Handle them where they occur; propagate with context.
4.  Prefer boring technology. New stack = new failure modes at 3 AM.
5.  Interfaces decouple. Implementations evolve. Design for the interface.
6.  Delete more than you add. The best line of code is one that doesn't exist.
7.  Tests document intent. If a test is hard to write, the design is wrong.
8.  Observability is a first-class feature. Build for the operator, not just the user.
9.  Every system will be distributed eventually. Design for partial failure now.
10. Toil is a bug. Automate repetitive operations or accept them as technical debt.
11. Own your dependencies. "It works on my machine" is an infrastructure problem.
12. The README is the API. Documentation is not optional — it is the contract.
13. Reversibility > optimality. Being able to undo beats being maximally efficient.
14. Latency compounds. Track p99, not averages. The tail is the user experience.
15. Security is not a layer. It is a property of every decision in the stack.
16. Schema changes are deployments. Migrate forward, never backward.
17. Feature flags are mandatory for risky rollouts. Dark launch first.
18. On-call is a design review. Every page is a failure of architecture or docs.
19. Logging !== observability. Correlate logs, metrics, and traces from day one.
20. Conway's Law is real. Your architecture mirrors your team structure.
21. Test at the right layer. Unit test logic, integration test seams, e2e test flows.
22. Immutable infrastructure over configuration drift. Rebuild, don't patch.
23. Least privilege everywhere. Every service, every secret, every role.
24. Fail fast, fail loudly. Silent failures are production landmines.
25. Context propagation is non-negotiable. Trace IDs in every log line.
```
